inshape: checks for register microdata

Source: R/inshape-package.R
inshape-package.Rd

Register microdata comes in a few shapes: one row per unit, one row per unit and period (a panel), or one row per spell with a start and an end. Every analysis assumes the shape is right: no duplicated persons, no missing years in the middle of a panel, no person with two addresses at once. inshape checks those assumptions, fast enough for full-population registers. See vignette("inshape").

Details

The name

Register data has a shape, and an analysis is written for one of them. inshape asks whether the data is in shape, the shape the analysis assumes: are the keys unique, the panels whole, the spells consistent, before anyone builds on them?

Where to start

  • describe_key(), describe_panel(), describe_spells(), describe_varying() and describe_codes(): look at the structure before choosing a rule.

  • describe_changes(): what changed since the last extract.

  • describe_match(): what a join of two tables will do, before it is made.

  • ensure_unique(): a key identifies each row.

  • ensure_complete(): the columns an analysis cannot do without have no missing values.

  • ensure_balanced(): every unit is observed in every period, or at least has no gaps.

  • ensure_valid_spells(): a spell has a start and does not end before it.

  • ensure_no_overlap(): a unit is in one spell at a time.

  • ensure_no_gaps(): and in one all the time, without a break between its spells.

  • ensure_constant(): sex, birth date and the like do not change within a unit.

  • ensure_within(): no one is observed after death or emigration, or before birth.

  • ensure_codes(): a coded column holds only codes from the code list, valid at the time of the row.

  • ensure_matched(): every key occurs in a reference register.

  • ensure_none(), ensure_all() and ensure_empty(): any other rule dplyr can express, such as no negative amounts.

  • tally_violations(): count many rules at once, without judging.

  • violations(): the rows that break a check, all of them.

  • merge_spells(): one spell recorded as several, merged into one.

  • spells_to_panel() and add_spell_status(): from spells to a panel.

The ensure_*() functions are checkpoints: they warn or abort with the offending rows and return the data, so they sit in a pipeline. What they share (messages, personal data, database tables) is described in checkpoints.

persons |>
  ensure_unique(cpr, year, abort_msg = "Duplicate person-years") |>
  ensure_balanced(cpr, year, gaps_only = TRUE)

gaps <- violations(ensure_balanced(persons, cpr, year, gaps_only = TRUE))

Why a package of its own

The checkpoints and the spell conversions started in the daos package. They moved here because they share an engine the rest of daos does not: the grouping of keys such as cpr without sorting them, the compiled pass over sorted spells, and one way of reporting a broken rule. The general checkpoints, ensure_none(), ensure_all(), ensure_empty() and tally_violations(), spent a while in the expectr package and joined the rest here, since they share the same contract, the same reporting and the same dependencies.
